q_paper_title: Carleson operators on doubling metric measure spaces
q_slogan: For a bounded, periodic, complex-valued function g, the absolute value of its N-th partial Fourier sum at any point is no more than the average of two transformed values of g and its complex conjugate, plus a term proportional to the bound on g.
c_slogan: For a periodic, measurable complex function g bounded by a positive number delta, the absolute value of its partial Fourier sum at any point in the interval [0, 2*pi] is no larger than the sum of two Carleson operators applied to g and its complex conjugate, divided by 2*pi, plus pi times delta.

q_slogan: For every linear map between representations of a group G over a ring R, applying the norm map NG before or after the linear map gives the same result. This means the norm map NG commutes with all such linear maps. In other words, NG acts as a natural transformation from the identity functor to itself on the category of G-representations over R.
c_slogan: For a finite group G and commutative ring R, if A and B are representations of G over R and φ is a G-equivariant linear map from A to B, then the norm map on B composed with φ equals φ composed with the norm map on A. This means the norm operation commutes with intertwiners between representations.

q_slogan: The set of nonnegative real numbers has a collection of subsets covering each interval [0,n) such that the number of sets needed to cover each interval grows in a controlled way, with bounds determined by the constants n and exponents 1.
c_slogan: The sets [0, n+1) for natural numbers n form a cover of the nonnegative real numbers, and each set has a covering number bounded by 3*(n+1) with respect to the constant scale function 1.

q_slogan: If two families of random variables are uniformly integrable, then the family formed by adding corresponding elements from each family is also uniformly integrable.
c_slogan: If two families of functions are uniformly integrable with respect to a measure and the exponent p is at least 1, then their sum is also uniformly integrable with respect to the same measure and exponent.
